intro: These three patterns all pair two items, A and B, but they do three different jobs. であれ says it makes no difference which one: the statement holds either way. といい picks two aspects of one thing as evidence for a judgement about the whole. なり offers two options and tells the listener to pick one and act. Ask which job the sentence is doing: regardless, judging, or choosing.

skills.rule: To say whether it is A or B (or whatever it is), the main clause holds all the same, use AであれBであれ, or にせよ / にしろ after verbs.
skills.explain:
であれ is the concessive form of である: even if it is A. Doubled, AであれBであれ means whether A or B. With a question word it means any at all: 何であれ (whatever it is), 誰であれ (whoever), どこであれ (wherever). The main clause is a fixed truth, duty or decision that the choice does not change: 理由が何であれ、遅刻はよくない.

であれ attaches to nouns and な-adjective stems. Verbs and い-adjectives take にせよ or にしろ instead, which do the same job: 行くにせよ行かないにせよ (whether you go or not). にせよ is the written, slightly formal one; にしろ is common in speech. Both also attach to nouns, so 大人にせよ子供にせよ is fine too. A single にせよ / にしろ means even if, granted that: 冗談にしろ、言うべきではない.

The edge: であれ dismisses the difference. If the speaker is praising or criticising one thing on two counts, that is といい. If the speaker is offering choices to act on, that is なり.
patterns: [noun A] であれ [noun B] であれ、[fixed conclusion]
何 / 誰 / どこ であれ、[fixed conclusion]
[verb] にせよ / にしろ [verb (neg.)] にせよ / にしろ、[conclusion]

examples.jp: 理由[りゆう]が何[なん]{であれ}、遅刻[ちこく]はよくない。
examples.en: Whatever the reason, being late is not acceptable.

examples.jp: 誰[だれ]{であれ}、この部屋[へや]に入[はい]るには許可[きょか]が必要[ひつよう]だ。
examples.en: Whoever you are, you need permission to enter this room.

examples.jp: 大人[おとな]{であれ}子供[こども]{であれ}、ルールは守[まも]らなければならない。
examples.en: Adult or child, everyone has to follow the rules.

examples.jp: 晴[は]れ{であれ}雨[あめ]{であれ}、試合[しあい]は予定[よてい]通[どお]り行[おこな]われる。
examples.en: Rain or shine, the match will go ahead as planned.

examples.jp: 行[い]く{にせよ}行[い]かない{にせよ}、明日[あした]までに返事[へんじ]をください。
examples.en: Whether you go or not, please let me know by tomorrow.

examples.jp: 冗談[じょうだん]{にしろ}、そんなことを言[い]うべきではない。
examples.en: Even as a joke, you shouldn't say something like that.

contrast.note: AといいBといい judges one thing by two of its aspects (味といい値段といい、最高だ). AであれBであれ says the conclusion holds whichever case applies; nothing is being praised.
AなりBなり offers options and asks someone to choose one (電話なりメールなりで連絡して). であれ offers no choice: it closes the question.
やら and だの list things that really exist or happened, often too many of them. であれ lists cases only to say the difference does not matter.

mistakes.bad: 行[い]く{であれ}行[い]かない{であれ}、連絡[れんらく]してください。
mistakes.good: 行[い]く{にせよ}行[い]かない{にせよ}、連絡[れんらく]してください。
mistakes.note: であれ follows nouns and な-adjective stems. Verbs take にせよ or にしろ.

mistakes.bad: 味[あじ]{であれ}値段[ねだん]{であれ}、この店[みせ]は最高[さいこう]だ。
mistakes.good: 味[あじ]{といい}値段[ねだん]{といい}、この店[みせ]は最高[さいこう]だ。
mistakes.note: Praising one restaurant on two counts is といい. であれ would mean regardless of taste or price, which makes no sense.

skills.tip: Can you translate it with whether A or B, it does not matter? Then であれ (nouns) or にせよ / にしろ (verbs).

skills.rule: To judge one person or thing by pointing at two of its aspects, say AといいBといい and then give the verdict on the whole.
skills.explain:
AといいBといい literally means if you speak of A, if you speak of B. The speaker picks two features of one subject as examples and then states a judgement that both features support: 味といい値段といい、この店は文句なしだ (in taste and in price alike, this place is perfect). It can also take two members of one group: 兄といい弟といい (both the older and the younger brother).

The verdict is evaluative and usually emotional: admiration (素晴らしい, 最高だ) or exasperation (失礼すぎる, あきれる). It covers the whole subject, not just one of the two features, so 味といい値段といい、安い fails: 安い only fits the price. A and B are nouns. The pattern is written and formal-leaning; in speech it adds a sense of the speaker summing up.

The edge: であれ is regardless, なり is pick one to act, やら is a messy list of what happened. Only といい evaluates.
patterns: [aspect A] といい [aspect B] といい、[subject] は [evaluation]
[person A] といい [person B] といい、[shared verdict]

examples.jp: 色[いろ]{といい}形[かたち]{といい}、このかばんは本当[ほんとう]に素敵[すてき]です。
examples.en: In colour and in shape alike, this bag is really lovely.

examples.jp: 味[あじ]{といい}値段[ねだん]{といい}、この店[みせ]は文句[もんく]なしだ。
examples.en: Both the food and the prices here are beyond complaint.

examples.jp: 景色[けしき]{といい}料理[りょうり]{といい}、最高[さいこう]の旅館[りょかん]でした。
examples.en: The view, the food, everything made it a perfect inn.

examples.jp: 態度[たいど]{といい}言葉遣[ことばづか]い{といい}、あの店員[てんいん]は失礼[しつれい]すぎる。
examples.en: Between the attitude and the way they talk, that clerk is far too rude.

examples.jp: 兄[あに]{といい}弟[おとうと]{といい}、あの家[いえ]の息子[むすこ]はみんな背[せ]が高[たか]い。
examples.en: The older one and the younger one alike, the sons in that family are all tall.

contrast.note: であれ means it does not matter which: the conclusion is indifferent to A or B. といい names A and B precisely because they matter: they are the evidence.
AやらBやら piles up things that happened, usually chaotic or tiring (宿題やら掃除やらで忙しい). It reports; といい evaluates.
なり offers options to act on. といい never asks anyone to do anything.

mistakes.bad: 味[あじ]{といい}値段[ねだん]{といい}、この店[みせ]は安[やす]い。
mistakes.good: 味[あじ]{といい}値段[ねだん]{といい}、この店[みせ]は文句[もんく]なしだ。
mistakes.note: The verdict must fit both aspects. Cheap describes only the price; give a judgement on the whole.

mistakes.bad: 電話[でんわ]{といい}メール{といい}、連絡[れんらく]してください。
mistakes.good: 電話[でんわ]{なり}メール{なり}で連絡[れんらく]してください。
mistakes.note: Offering ways to get in touch is a choice to act on, which is なり. といい only evaluates.

skills.tip: Is a verdict coming about one thing, backed by two of its features? Then といい.

skills.rule: To offer the listener two example options and tell them to pick one and act, say AなりBなり.
skills.explain:
AなりBなり lists two possibilities as examples of what someone could do; the listener picks one, or something similar. The main clause is almost always a request, suggestion, order or intention: 電話なりメールなりで連絡してください (by phone, email, whatever). With verbs it is VなりVなりする: 座るなり横になるなりしてください (sit down or lie down, whichever).

The set phrase AなりなんなりB means A or anything like it: 水なりなんなり持ってきて (bring water or something). Because it hands over a choice, it is used about the future, not to report past facts, and it can sound a little directive, so it is said to equals and juniors more than to superiors.

The edge: とか gives casual examples in any context, including the past. であれ says the choice does not matter to a fixed conclusion. たり lists actions that were or are done. Only なり means pick one and do it.
patterns: [noun A] なり [noun B] なり (で / に) [request]
[verb A] なり [verb B] なり して [request / suggestion]

examples.jp: 電話[でんわ]{なり}メール{なり}で連絡[れんらく]してください。
examples.en: Please get in touch by phone, email, whatever suits you.

examples.jp: 分[わ]からなければ、先生[せんせい]{なり}先輩[せんぱい]{なり}に聞[き]いてみてください。
examples.en: If you don't understand, ask a teacher or one of the seniors.

examples.jp: 疲[つか]れたなら、座[すわ]る{なり}横[よこ]になる{なり}してください。
examples.en: If you're tired, sit down or lie down, whichever.

examples.jp: 図書館[としょかん]{なり}自宅[じたく]{なり}、静[しず]かな所[ところ]で勉強[べんきょう]しなさい。
examples.en: Study somewhere quiet, the library or at home.

examples.jp: 週末[しゅうまつ]は映画[えいが]を見[み]る{なり}散歩[さんぽ]する{なり}して、ゆっくり休[やす]みなさい。
examples.en: At the weekend, watch a film or go for a walk or something, and get some rest.

contrast.note: とか gives casual examples and works for past facts (昨日は買い物とか料理とかした). なり only proposes options for an action yet to be chosen.
AであれBであれ, X: X holds either way, nobody chooses. AなりBなり, X: choose one of them and do X.
やら lists a jumble of things that happened (雨やら風やらで大変だった). なり never describes what happened.

mistakes.bad: 昨日[きのう]は本[ほん]を読[よ]む{なり}テレビを見[み]る{なり}した。
mistakes.good: 昨日[きのう]は本[ほん]を読[よ]ん{だり}テレビを見[み]{たり}した。
mistakes.note: Listing what you actually did is たり. なり offers choices for the future.

mistakes.bad: 雨[あめ]{なり}風[かぜ]{なり}、ひどい一日[いちにち]だった。
mistakes.good: 雨[あめ]{やら}風[かぜ]{やら}、ひどい一日[いちにち]だった。
mistakes.note: A messy pile of things that happened is やら. Nobody is choosing between rain and wind.

skills.tip: Does the sentence end in a request or suggestion and mean pick one of these? Then なり.
